# Section 040: Measuring Platform Efficiency

Makes the reader able to measure how well the platform delivers and how well it uses resources: the four DORA metrics from GitOps history, service level objectives with error budgets, and the gap between requested and used CPU and memory. It comes after the collection sections because every number here is a Prometheus query on data those sections taught to collect.

**Curriculum item covered:** Measuring and Improving Platform Efficiency Using Deployment Metrics and Performance Indicators

---

## What You Will Master

- Define deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate and time to restore service
- Count deployments over a time window from the GitOps controller's sync metrics in Prometheus
- Calculate lead time from a commit time in Git and the sync time recorded by the controller
- Calculate change failure rate and time to restore from failed and recovered deployments
- Name one change to the delivery process that improves each metric
- Write an SLI as a PromQL ratio of good requests to all requests
- Calculate the remaining error budget for a 99% SLO over a window
- Write a burn-rate alert that fires when the budget would run out early
- Compare container CPU and memory requests with real usage from metrics-server and Prometheus
- Name the workload with the biggest gap and change its requests to match usage

---

## The Learning Path

### 1. Measure Delivery With DORA Metrics
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 1: Measure Delivery With DORA Metrics](./module-01/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-040/module-01/playground` — kind cluster with Gitea 28.1.0 holding a `starfleet-deploy` repository, Argo CD 3.5.4 with an Application for `scout` in `starfleet`, and trimmed Prometheus scraping Argo CD's metrics. A seed script makes a history of about ten commits and syncs, two of them deliberately bad (failing image tag) and later rolled back, so the queries have data. Flux is not installed. Heaviest playground in the course; nothing else runs beside it.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS020.git -c sections/section-040/module-01/playground
    ```

### 2. Measure Service Levels And Resource Efficiency
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 2: Measure Service Levels And Resource Efficiency](./module-02/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-040/module-02/playground` — kind cluster with metrics-server 0.9.0 and trimmed kube-prometheus-stack with kube-state-metrics on (needed for requests). `probe` serves a fixed share of 500 responses so the SLI is below target and the error budget is burning. `scout` requests far more CPU and memory than it uses, and a third Deployment requests too little, so both directions of the gap are visible.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS020.git -c sections/section-040/module-02/playground
    ```

### Section Capstone Challenge
*   **Comprehensive Challenge:** Platform Efficiency Capstone — `sections/section-040/capstone/labs/lab-01` *(created in the build phase)*
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS020.git -c sections/section-040/capstone/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```
*   **Hands-on Objective:** The platform team must report on `starfleet`. The reader writes recording rules for deployment frequency and change failure rate over the seeded history, an SLO error-budget recording rule and burn-rate alert for `probe`, and right-sizes the most over-requested Deployment. The grader queries the recorded series, checks the alert definition, and compares the new requests with measured usage.
